title: Potassium hydroxide on (110) silicon etches crystal-perfect vertical cell walls
idea: Align lines along <112> on (110) Si and etch in KOH so the slow {111} planes form atomically smooth vertical walls 20-40 nm thick at >100:1 aspect ratio; a deposited oxide/TiN wordline stack crossing the walls turns each wall into a vertical string of DRAM cells.
why: Single-crystal vertical semiconductor sheets for stacked cells (fact 2) without DRIE or EUV (fact 4), from a heated beaker; smooth walls trim the interface-trap leakage tail (fact 3).
note: Ultra-high-AR {111} KOH walls are proven in MEMS; novel as DRAM channel sheets, but capacitor placement is unaddressed.

title: GPU-owned sense amps: array stack bonded straight onto accelerator
idea: Limit: no base die and no DRAM-process periphery. Array-only layers with 8:1 bitline muxes are hybrid-bonded at fine pitch directly onto the accelerator die. Sense amps, decoders and controllers are built in the accelerator's 3 nm logic, at about 1/4 the area of DRAM-process periphery.
why: Facts 5 and 7: removes the HBM PHY and base die; data movement drops toward 0.3 pJ/bit and array dies become near-100% cells.
note: Building DRAM periphery in accelerator logic removes base die; 3 nm devices cannot drive boosted wordline voltages.

title: Correlated double sampling sense amps read 0.2 fF cells
idea: Sample the bitline before and after charge sharing onto two capacitors in a logic-process sense amp and amplify the difference, cancelling offset and 1/f noise so the required signal approaches the sqrt(kT/C) floor instead of a 6-sigma mismatch margin.
why: First principles: sqrt(kT/C) for a 30 fF bitline is ~0.37 mV, so ~3 mV suffices versus ~80-100 mV today; Cs can fall from ~5 fF to ~0.2-0.5 fF, dissolving the charge wall (fact 1) and enabling lateral capacitors in 3D (fact 2).
note: CDS sense amp targets kT/C floor so Cs drops ~10x; doubt: WL/BL coupling and charge injection, not thermal noise, set the floor.

title: Magnify contributors: open-source 3D DRAM compiler and PDK
idea: Fund three engineers to release an open-source array generator for SKY130 and GF180, plus a parametric 3D DRAM tier model (tier count, Cs, leakage tail, spares) and a cost and yield calculator, so universities can tape out DRAM arrays on open shuttles.
why: U.S. manufacturability and talent: brings hundreds of designers to array architecture for about $900k.

title: HP's The Machine fixed: pooled memory racks with a refurbishment loop
idea: HPE's The Machine died betting on an unready memristor. Build the same memory-centric fabric with today's DRAM in CXL-attached pooled racks, sold as a service. Modules are hot-swapped, tested, refurbished and redeployed to lower tiers instead of retiring with the server.
why: Pooling cuts stranded DRAM (often 20-40% unused per server), and refurbishment roughly doubles module life, raising usable supply without new fabs.

title: ZettaCore's molecular redox storage repurposed as a charge-multiplying capacitor coating
idea: ZettaCore stored charge in porphyrin redox molecules on silicon but died on the 400C BEOL thermal budget. Graft thermally stable inorganic redox clusters (polyoxometalates) inside each 3D DRAM capacitor. Each cluster stores several electrons at a fixed potential, adding pseudocapacitance on top of the dielectric's.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 5-10x charge per um2 lets 3D tiers use short, low-AR capacitors (fact 2).
note: Redox clusters multiply charge per area; doubt: ns-scale Faradaic kinetics, retention, and endurance.

title: Retrofit US flexible-packaging converting lines into memory-foil fabs
idea: Partner with U.S. label and flexible-packaging converters, whose vacuum web metallizers, slot-die coaters and gravure units already run at km per hour, add enclosed ISO-5 web paths plus nanoimprint and spatial-ALD modules, and sell memory foil per square metre under a tolling model.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability: a converted line costs ~$20-100M versus $15B+ for a DRAM fab, uses no EUV, no Czochralski wafers (no quartz-crucible chokepoint) and little helium, and can start within ~18 months in existing U.S. plants.
note: Converted web lines slash capex; doubt: web-processed devices reaching DRAM density, speed and particle-free yield.

title: Snack-bag web metallizers vacuum-coat 128-tier stacks by the kilometer
idea: Borrowed from roll-to-roll metallizers that coat packaging film at ~1,000 m/min: deposit 128 alternating Mo/SiOx wordline/insulator layers on a heat-tolerant web in multi-drum passes, laminate the stack onto a CMOS wafer, then one hole etch plus ALD finishes vertical-channel gain cells.
why: Tier-stack deposition is a dominant 3D cost; web coating is ~100x cheaper per m2, and with one mask for all tiers the path reaches ~$0.1/GB; trade-offs: lamination voids, lower tier quality, refresh-heavy cells.
note: Web-coated tier stacks could slash deposition cost; pinholes, lamination voids and etching through a web are the doubts.

title: Roll a 2D array film into a multi-turn scroll
idea: Turn area into tiers by rolling instead of stacking: fabricate a thin-film oxide DRAM array on a strained bilayer membrane with the existing mask set, then use one added release mask so the film self-rolls into a 10-30 turn Swiss roll, with turns connected through contacts at the scroll edge.
why: Density and 3D cost (facts 2,4): 10-30x bits per footprint without per-tier processing; rolled-up nanomembrane capacitors already exist.
note: 10-30 tiers from one patterned film; doubt: connecting inner turns and yield of rolled arrays.

title: Room-temperature single-electron electrometer at every vertical bitline foot
idea: Coulomb blockade: a sub-3 nm silicon island single-electron transistor, formed by self-limiting fin oxidation, sits at the base of each vertical bitline as a charge electrometer that can resolve ~10 electrons. Lateral 3D tier capacitors can then hold 0.2 fF instead of 5 fF, because the read no longer depends on charge-sharing against a large bitline capacitance.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) that blocks thin 3D tiers (fact 2); claim 20x smaller Cs, so planar tier capacitors become viable.
note: RT Coulomb-blockade readout could cut Cs 20x; doubt: sub-3 nm island variability and offset charge across billions of bitlines.

title: Drum-era SOAP placement makes shift-register memories act random-access
idea: Revive the IBM 650's Symbolic Optimal Assembly Program, which placed each next instruction where the rotating drum would be when needed: a compiler/controller lays out tensors, KV-cache pages and weights in shift-register arrays (CCD strings, racetracks, delay loops) so the next word reaches the read port just in time, with out-of-order prefetch hiding the rest.
why: Lets transistor-free serial 3D arrays serve the predictable ~60-80% of AI memory traffic at effective 10-30 ns latency, unlocking 5-10x denser arrays for DRAM's job.

title: Band-offset quantum-well bits stacked along a superlattice pillar
idea: Worse: store each bit on a bulky capacitor needing femtofarads. Flip: etch vertical pillars through a Si/Ge-rich superlattice, wrap each Ge-rich well with a tier gate, and store holes in its valence-band well (up to ~0.5 eV offset) as the bit, sensed as a threshold shift of the shared vertical Si channel, which is capacitorless and has no oxide tunneling, so endurance stays unlimited.
why: Every tier of every pillar is a bit: 128 tiers at 50 nm pillar pitch is ~17 nm2/bit (~50x), so 10x survives even at 20% array efficiency with NAND-like process cost; retention from thermal emission over the band offset is the speculative part.
note: Capacitorless bit per tier gives ~50x density; doubt: 0.5 eV offset means ~us retention at 85C, not ms.
